messages:
tara_support: Customer reported SSE connection dropping with a 401 right after our token rotation window. Request ID: req-981234. Need a minimal cURL repro and which headers to validate. They said it works for a few minutes then 401 on the next event.

sam_m: can you paste the exact curl they tried? often missing Accept or wrong cookie header name.

tara_support: here's the snippet they used (redacted token). I edited to keep it minimal — still reproduces on our side once rotation happens:

```bash
curl -i -N \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Cookie: session=REDACTED_SESSION; path=/; HttpOnly" \\n  -H "X-Request-ID: req-981234" \\n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-lite"
```

sam_m: that looks reasonable. add `--no-buffer` and `-v` so we can capture the headers handshake and any Set-Cookie on the response. also try `--raw` to avoid curl mangling chunked SSE.

kai_infra: also run with `--trace-ascii curl_trace.txt` (or `--trace`) to get wire-level details. if the 401 happens right after rotation, watch for a `Set-Cookie` or `Set-Authorization` header on the server side — maybe rotation writes a cookie that the client doesn't persist. check `Set-Cookie` expiry.

jess_ops: make sure to capture the request/response headers plus the process time for rotation. Steps for debug bundle:
- run curl with `-v --no-buffer --trace-ascii trace.txt`
- save the server side request logs for `req-981234` and +/- 2 minutes
- include the orchestration rotation timestamp (approx 15:02 UTC)
- redact tokens before upload (replace bearer and cookie values with REDACTED)

escalation-bot: Reminder: include the following in the bundle: `trace.txt`, `curl_output.txt`, server logs for req-981234, and the token-rotation event time. Mark as P2 if customer impact > 10 users.

tara_support: got it. one more ask — is there a preferred header we should insist customers include to help correlate? we already added X-Request-ID.

sam_m: X-Request-ID is perfect. also suggest they send `X-Client-Timestamp` (epoch ms) so we can align client timeline vs server rotation. if you can, capture both `Set-Cookie` and any `Authorization` header in the response.

kai_infra: quick checklist for reproduction: 
1) start curl with the headers above and `--trace-ascii`
2) trigger token rotation (or wait the 5–10m window)
3) observe first 401 event and save the trace
4) check if curl received a `Set-Cookie` that it ignored or if server responded with a new `WWW-Authenticate` header

jess_ops: if they can't reproduce reliably, ask them to run a small loop that reconnects on 401 and logs the full handshake. example loop we suggest in support doc: 
```bash
while true; do 
  curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \\n    -H "X-Request-ID: $(date +%s)-local" 
  sleep 1
done
```

tara_support: perfect, I'll collect the `trace.txt` + `curl_output.txt` + our server logs and drop a redacted bundle here. will include token rotation timestamp and X-Client-Timestamp. thanks both :thumbsup:

escalation-bot: Noted — created escalation ticket E-2026-384 for follow-up.

sam_m: once you have the bundle ping me and I'll run the trace against infra logs to see if rotation invalidated the previous session cookie.

tara_support: will do — uploading in ~15m. thanks everyone.
